summary: Mars Base Survival: Junior Trainer is a hands-on, non-digital board game combined with a 3D LEGO Mars Base model. Designed for young learners, the game simulates real challenges on Mars—such as solar storms, toxic perchlorate soil, 95% CO₂ atmosphere, and 20-minute radio communication delays with Earth. Players manage four essential resources (Oxygen, Power, Food, and Shielding) across five scientific base zones and draw Mission Cards to solve real Martian emergencies, turning complex space science into fun, interactive learning. More than just a game, Mars Base Survival: Junior Trainer turns the dream of exploring Mars into a hands-on scientific adventure, inspiring the next generation of space explorers."
details:
Mars Base Survival: Junior Trainer is an educational board game that teaches young learners how to survive on Mars. Players manage four essential resources: Oxygen, Power, Food, and Shielding. They explore five scientific base zones and draw Mission Cards to solve realistic Martian emergencies, such as solar storms, toxic soil, and communication delays with Earth.

The project makes learning about space science more fun, accessible, and interactive. It helps children develop critical thinking, problem-solving, teamwork, decision-making, and resource management skills while gaining basic knowledge about Mars and space exploration.We used LEGO bricks to build a 3D model of the Mars Base and designed a physical board game with resource tokens, game zones, and Mission Cards. The project focuses on hands-on, non-digital learning, allowing players to interact directly with the game materials without requiring computers or electronic devices.

Our project creatively combines a traditional board game with a 3D LEGO Mars Base model. Instead of simply reading about space science, players experience the challenges of surviving on Mars through interactive missions and resource management. It transforms complex scientific concepts into an exciting and easy-to-understand learning experience for children.Our team considered scientific accuracy, educational value, age-appropriate design, gameplay balance, and ease of use. We included realistic Martian environmental conditions, such as solar storms, toxic perchlorate soil, a 95% CO₂ atmosphere, and communication delays with Earth. We also focused on making the game safe, engaging, affordable, and easy for young learners to understand and play.
